newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's counsels Philippines banks to be cautious.
newsitem.headline: Moody's counsels Philippines banks to be cautious.

text.p: Philippines banks should maintain a cautious and prudent approach to business to avoid problems that accompany excessive growth, Moody's Investors Service said in a report.

Moody's said it was concerned that Philippines banks' conservative approach "may give way to a less cautious approach to business, as the euphoria of the Philippines' significant improvement in economic management of the last five years attenuates the need to exercise prudence and caution.

"The risk is that the Philippine banks (and corporates) may end up paying the same price of excessive growth and leverage that some other Asian banking systems are paying -- notably Thailand, Korea and Japan -- after the 'bubble economy' bursts," the rating agency said in the report.

Moody's said the biggest challenge for the Philippines may be to restrain growth, especially in potentially vulnerable sectors such as some segments of the real estate market and consumer lending, and in products such as credit cards and auto lending.
But Moody's also said that, broadly speaking, the profitablity, asset quality, earnings and capital levels of Philippine banks compared favourably with those of other banks in the region.
Moody's rates the Philippines' foreign currency bonds at Ba2 and its foreign currency bank deposits at Ba3. In January 1997, Moody's put these ratings on review for possible upgrade.
In line with the sovereign review, Moody's also said it might raise the debt ratings of 11 Philippine banks.
